title: Hubble image of NGC 1073
caption: The barred spiral galaxy NGC 1073, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: IXO 5, J024333.6+012222, NGC 1073, PKS 0241+011, QSO B0240+011, VV96 · constellation Cetus · about 55 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble image shows NGC 1073, a barred spiral galaxy in the constellation of Cetus, the Sea Monster. It lies about 55 million light-years away.
A barred spiral is a spiral galaxy with a straight band of stars across its middle, and the spiral arms wind outward from the ends of that bar.

NGC 1073 has a special interest for us. The Milky Way, our home galaxy, is also thought to be a barred spiral. Because we sit inside the Milky Way's disc, we can never step outside to see its overall shape. Studying galaxies like NGC 1073 from the outside gives astronomers a way to learn more about the structure of our own galaxy, using a similar galaxy as a stand-in for the one we cannot photograph.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.24 x 2.56 arcminutes) and distance (55 million light years), the frame spans roughly 52,000 × 41,000 light-years. Its light set out about 55 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using blue and visible filters. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The galaxy is far too faint to see this way without a telescope, and Hubble's exposures collect much more light than an eye can.
